dimensions.reason: N072 5.3-5.5 designates Business System Owners and the CIO (for shared Digital Resources) with power to suspend access or cease operations, and N067 5.2 designates the Privacy Office, though no unified cross-system authority governs standing AI-agent delegation across academic and administrative platforms.

documents_checked.text:
5.3 Business System Owners are responsible for —
(a) understanding the Cyber Security Risk Rating and related requirements of University Digital
Resources within their area of responsibility;
(b) ensuring that University Digital Resources are not acquired or implemented within their area of
responsibility without prior input and authorisation by University IT;
(c) allocating sufficient resources and support for their University Digital Resources to have all
controls designed, acquired, implemented, operated, and maintained in accordance with the
Cyber Security Framework;
(d) identifying, reporting, owning and managing Cyber Security risks associated with their University
Digital Resources and related third party suppliers, vendors and partners;
(e) supporting the University IT Cyber Security Function in delivering the Cyber Security Strategy and
when conducting Cyber Security reviews; and
(f) where deemed necessary, formally assign management of University Digital Resources within
their area of responsibility to Technical System Owners or retain associated responsibilities.

5.5 Chief Information Officer will be responsible for —
(a) acting as Business System Owner for shared University Digital Resources that are not directly
attributable to a single business capability;
(b) allocating sufficient resources and support for managing Cyber Security risks;
(c) suspending access to University Digital Resources by members of the University Community
where such access —
i. risks causing a major Cyber Security incident; or
ii. constitute unauthorised non-compliance with requirements of the Cyber Security
Framework.
(d) taking steps to cease any University Digital Resource operation or activity that —
i. risks causing a major Cyber Security incident; or
ii. constitute unauthorised non-compliance with requirements of the Cyber Security
Framework.

5.2 Privacy Complaints
(a) The University will investigate and take seriously complaints made by individuals relating to the
University’s handling and management of Personal Information, including disclosure of their
information, where that is contrary to this Policy, or an interference with their privacy in accordance
with the PRIS Act.
(b) Complaints must be submitted in writing to the UWA Privacy Office (privacy@uwa.edu.au) and
include sufficient details of the Personal Information concerned, and the conduct alleged to be
inconsistent with this Policy or constitutes an interference with privacy.
(c) Privacy Complaints made to the UWA Privacy Office under 5.1(b) above will be dealt with as soon
as practical but where possible within 45 University working days.

4.4 Automated Decision Making (ADM)
When the University employs an ADM process involving the use of Personal Information that is used in
making Significant Decisions about individuals, the University must:
(a) Conduct and document an impact assessment that considers how to minimise the risk of harm,
bias and discrimination;
(b) Notify individuals that it is using ADM and, on request, provide information about how the ADM
process works; and
(c) Provide a process through which individuals can request human involvement in the decision.

4.5 Monitoring and Continual Improvement
(a) A Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to identify privacy risks and measures to mitigate them must
be undertaken by the University where a new process or system involving personal information is
implemented or existing process changed that could reasonably have a significant impact on the
privacy of individuals.
(b) The University monitors, measures, analyses and evaluates information privacy compliance
performance, controls and processes to ensure they are and remain appropriate and effective.

Breach Policy.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Purpose-bounded authorisation for combined standing powers, with security, intervention and contestability of consequential actions.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Under Protocol v1.1 (adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15), while N071 and N072 provide least-privilege security and CIO suspension powers, UWA lacks a unified purpose-bounded authorisation and per-action contestability framework for an AI agent exercising combined standing powers across LMS, enrolment, advising, and assessment systems.
case_summary.case_note: UWA Acceptable Use of IT Policy N071 enforces least-privilege access and bans credential sharing for automated agents, while Cyber Security Policy N072 empowers the CIO to suspend risky Digital Resource operations. However, UWA lacks a unified purpose-bounded authorisation and per-action contestability framework for standing AI powers spanning LMS, enrolment, advising, and assessment systems, leaving a critical gap. Note that Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
